summary: LDAP bridge timestamp unit mismatch causes RBAC reconciliation to skip recent group changes
description:
Issue summary:
After a deployment of the new LDAP bridge (v2.3.4) on 2026-03-12 02:40 UTC, multiple users reported that recently granted Okta group memberships were not reflected in Redwood RBAC. The reconciliation job appears to skip group updates that the bridge just wrote.

Impact:
- Several oncall and infra service accounts did not receive elevated roles for ~30-90 minutes after group changes.
- Affected internal consoles: analytics-portal, observability-runbooks, infra-deploy.
- Users experienced 403s when attempting role-elevation flows and just-in-time access.

Environment:
- prod - us-west (identity-sync cluster ids: id-sync-3, id-sync-4)
- LDAP bridge v2.3.4 (new release, change: timestamp serialization refactor)

Steps to reproduce:
1. In Okta, add a test user (jdoe-test) to the "oncall-rotate" group via the admin UI.
2. Observe SCIM/LDAP provisioning logs in identity-bridge.
3. Trigger RBAC reconciliation (manually via /admin/reconcile or wait for periodic job).
4. Check user role assignment in Redwood console and test elevation flows.

Observed behavior:
- identity-bridge logs show group update events with lastUpdated=1650001234567
- RBAC reconciler treats timestamps as epoch seconds; when it parses 1650001234567 it interprets as 1.650001234567e+12 seconds (far future), causing the reconciler to mark the record as "not ready for reconciliation" and skip processing.
- Reconciliation resumes only after a periodic backstop that clamps dates, causing ~30–90m delay.

Expected behavior:
- Timestamps from the LDAP bridge should be serialized in seconds (1650001234) or reconciler should robustly detect ms vs s. Group changes should be applied within normal reconcile window (<30s).

Logs / Evidence:
- identity-bridge id-sync-3 log excerpt (2026-03-12T02:42:11Z): "groupChange: user=jdoe-test group=oncall-rotate lastUpdated=1650001234567"
- rbac-reconciler log (2026-03-12T02:45:05Z): "skip: incoming_ts > future_threshold: 1650001234567"
- User ticket: several 403 screenshots attached in support thread #support (Slack).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 03:10 - Ravi: Pulled bridge container image diff; recent refactor changed time.Now().UnixNano() / 1e6 -> wrote raw UnixNano into JSON; unit mismatch introduced (ms vs s).
2026-03-12 03:35 - SRE: Confirmed reconciler codebase assumes seconds (int64) and lacks guardrails for >1e11 values; unit test coverage missing for extreme timestamp values.
2026-03-12 04:05 - Maya: Correlated user reports with deployment timeframe; pattern holds: all affected users had group events written by id-sync-3/id-sync-4 between 02:40-03:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 05:00 - Security: Verified no privilege escalation occurred; delay caused temporary denial for intended role holders but no unauthorized grants.
comments: 2026-03-12 03:20 - Ravi Patel (assignee): Created a hotfix branch to normalize timestamps on write and added defensive parsing on read. PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-bridge/pull/1287

2026-03-12 03:55 - Maya Chen (reporter): Rolled temporary mitigation by restarting id-sync-3 to pick older image (v2.3.3). Observed reconciler catch-up beginning at 03:10 UTC — several users became active again.
2026-03-12 04:30 - SRE oncall (Anjali Rao): Deployed reconciler patch to tolerate ms timestamps (clamps >1e11 to ms->s conversion) as a safety measure; added metric to track 'future_ts_skips'.

2026-03-12 12:15 - Ravi Patel: Merged hotfix to main and scheduled canary rollout. Notifying partner teams to watch for residual delays; filing follow-up to add unit tests and schema validation to bridge.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Product Ops (Liam Ortiz): Confirmed with affected teams that all outstanding elevation requests are cleared; no further user reports after full rollout.
resolution: Mitigated: rolled back the id-sync-3 instance to v2.3.3 to stop new malformed timestamps. Deployed immediate reconciler tolerant parse for ms values to prevent future skips. Hotfix merged into identity-bridge (PR #1287) and rolled out to prod canary on 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC, full rollout 2026-03-12 11:30 UTC. Follow-up: add strict timestamp schema validation in bridge, add unit tests for ms/vs-s handling, and create alert on 'future_ts_skips' metric.
